Summary: HighTide builds a cloud-native agent desktop for mid-size contact centers; evaluating Redwood for live agent assist and burst-resilient routing. Primary ask: streaming suggestions with strict guardrails and demonstrable SLOs during marketing/retention spikes.

Key contact: Lina Gomez (Head of CX Platforms) – strong bias toward deterministic latencies and enterprise-grade auditability. Quote from discovery call: 'If a suggestion shows up late, it does more harm than good.'

Technical requirements (from discovery):
- Real-time streaming suggestions to agent UI (per-suggestion arrival target: 95th < 200ms from user keystroke to first token).
- Summarization service for end-of-interaction tickets: batch summary TTL < 5s, 99th < 10s.
- Tool-calling integrations: CRM update, ticket tagging, outbound webhook calls; require idempotency and tracing headers.
- Guardrails: strict hallucination controls, allowlist/blocklist for PII and escalation triggers to supervisor.
- Spike handling: expected peak concurrency 300 agents in NA region, occasional bursts to 900 for scheduled campaigns; must preserve tail latency and fallback to lower-cost model variant without dropping session state.

Security/compliance notes: SOC2 required, SSO (SAML + SCIM), customer-managed KMS preferred for Dedicated/Private, audit log retention for 1 year (configurable). Legal flagged data residency for EU customers (possible future requirement).

POC scope agreed in principle (6 weeks):
- Week 0–1: env prep, IP allowlist, SAML test, sample dataset transfer (anonymized transcripts).
- Week 2–4: integrate streaming API into agent app + routing policy test (canary to 10% of agents).
- Week 5: run synthetic burst tests (spike to 900 agents) and capture tail latencies, throughput, error modes.
- Week 6: finalize acceptance criteria: suggestion latency metrics, suggestion acceptance rate uplift, reduction in average handle time.

Success metrics they care about: suggestion acceptance rate +15%, handle time reduction 8–12%, faults <0.5% during spikes. Cost sensitivity: willing to pay for reserved capacity for predictable spikes; wants Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching & quantization to shave per-token cost.
